content.text:
Reviewed all 50 verbs in shard 1 and wrote `verbdata/gloss-review/shards/gloss_001.out.json` with 5 findings, all `medium`:

| Verb | Shipped | Proposed |
|---|---|---|
| `abrichten` | drill | train (an animal) |
| `abstechen` | cut off, cut out, carve out | stab to death |
| `absterben` | atrophy | die off, die back |
| `abtreiben` | go/be sent off course | have an abortion |
| `abtreten` | kick away | step down, cede |

`★ Insight ─────────────────────────────────────`
- This shard is almost entirely *ab-* verbs, and that concentrates a specific failure mode: *ab-* is one of German's most productive prefixes, so its verbs are heavily polysemous, and kaikki's entry order tends to lead with the concrete, physical reading (cut off with a spade, kick away, drift off course) while the sense that actually circulates is abstract or idiomatic. Four of my five findings are that exact shape.
- `absterben` is the one that isn't a sense-ordering defect — it's an English-side error. "Atrophy" and "die" are different biological claims (wasting from disuse vs. cell death), so the gloss is wrong even though it landed in the right semantic field. Worth noting that this class can't be caught by any `sense_index` heuristic.
- I deliberately did not flag several that looked suspicious on first pass — `abschießen` "shoot off", `absetzen` "depose, discontinue", `abstreiten` "repudiate", `abwandern` "emigrate". Each is thin or formal rather than wrong, and the brief is explicit that incomplete costs less than a false positive.
`─────────────────────────────────────────────────`

Rate is 10%, above the ~5% baseline, which I'd attribute to the prefix clustering rather than to a looser bar.
